Raw per-sample immunopeptidomics quality metrics

Source: R/quality-score.R
qc_metrics_by_sample.Rd

Computes, for each Sample in a pep_all table, the raw (un-scored) quality signals consumed by score_sample_quality(). Every metric is derived from the unified pep_all schema with no external data.

Usage

qc_metrics_by_sample(pep_all, shortpep_range = c(8, 13), mhcclass = "MHC1")

Arguments

pep_all

A unified pep_all data frame (see the package's pep_all schema): one row per peptide-sample observation, with at least Sample, Peptide, Sequence, Length, Cter, Charge, Accession and (optionally) ppm.

shortpep_range

Length-2 numeric c(min, max): the biologically expected ligand-length window (e.g. c(8, 13) for HLA-I, c(12, 25) for HLA-II).

mhcclass

"MHC1", "MHC1_mouse" or "MHC2". For "MHC2" the canonical-length and anchor-motif metrics are returned as NA (no fixed-length anchor model), so they drop out of the composite downstream — frac_nested_core is the class-II motif dimension instead, and quality_thresholds_default() gives it the anchor metric's weight there. For "MHC1_mouse", frac_9mer counts 8- and 9-mers (both canonical for murine H-2) and the anchor motif is scored on whichever of the two the sample has more of. frac_charge_1_2 is the fraction of in-window observations at a plausible charge: 1+/2+ for MHC-I (and custom windows), but 2+ to 4+ for "MHC2", whose 12-25-mers are rarely singly charged. The key is the same for every class.

Value

A data frame with one row per Sample and columns: frac_in_window, frac_9mer, frac_cterm_KR, frac_cterm_KR_longonly, anchor_information, frac_nested_core, median_abs_rt_error, median_abs_im_error, frac_cross_class, frac_charge_1_2, n_unique_pep, n_unique_pep_in_window, n_source_proteins, median_abs_ppm.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
qc_metrics_by_sample(pep_all, shortpep_range = c(8, 13), mhcclass = "MHC1")
} # }
